data.title: Notification
data.tagline: Notify the user about an event with a title and details
data.description: A notification carries more information than a toast and suits background jobs, activity from other people, and delayed results. If the message should be available later, also store it in a notification center with a read state.

use: An event that may need later review
avoid: Use it for every tiny local action
Show it once when the information must remain available
Hide the source or time of the event
Send repeated notifications for the same unchanged state

lessonPractice.title: A user starts a report export and leaves the page. The file becomes ready five minutes later. How should completion be communicated?

options.label: Create a notification that can be revisited, with the file name and download action
options.feedback: The result occurs after the original action and needs follow-up, so a retained notification lets users find the exact file later.

options.label: Show Export complete for two seconds on the original page and then dismiss it
options.feedback: The user already left that page, so brief feedback may never be seen and provides no later download path.

options.label: Open a non-dismissible modal on the user's current page and require an immediate download
options.feedback: Export completion does not block the current task. Forced handling turns a background task into an interruption.

data.agentPrompt: When a background export finishes, add a notification with the report name, completion time, download action, and clear unread state. Do not rely on a toast on the original page or block the current page. Verify it survives navigation.
